The Grand Royal Vision for Stability and Prosperity

Under the quick and decisive guidance of His Majesty King Rama IX, the transitional period was completed with minimal issues. The military junta cooperated fully with His Majesty’s request and was rewarded with positions high in the new government. Not all were happy but with support of the Junta any dissenters were quickly found and ejected from places of power. Several members of the Junta, among them General Prayut Chan-o-cha, Commander of the Royal Thai Army and leader of the most recent coup, were placed within the Privy Council and directly advise the King.

Over the past weeks His Majesty, the Privy Council and trusted experts have worked together to develop what has been called my His Majesty the “Grand Royal Vision for Stability and Prosperity.” The Grand Royal Vision outlines a number of priorities and programs that will address the systemic issues within his kingdom. The current plan will focus on four main areas, manufacturing, agriculture, education and military as well as several smaller reforms that work to address internal issues within the government.

Manufacturing

Thailand’s economy is heavily based in the manufacturing industry in Thailand which accounts for approximately 45% of the GDP, several new programs to make Thailand more attractive to manufacturers have been put in place. A number of tax breaks and incentives will be made available to new industries moving their operations to Thailand. Additionally, a program started by the Junta to build new rail links with China to improve trade between the regions will be continued.

Agriculture

Approximately 50% of the working population within Thailand operate within the agricultural industry, Thailand has a great deal of arable land in the form of rice paddies and is the largest producer of rice in the world. Coming off from the Yingluck administration and the Junta several programs have been put in place already to subsidize the rice farmers. These programs were expensive and largely considered a failure. Rice prices dropped and the program which purchased the rice at an inflated rate resulted in massive government stockpiles of rice which had to be sold at a loss. These programs will be stopped at a savings of approx. 5 Billion USD per year. New programs to redevelop the current rice fields into more profitable crops such as corn, potatoes, peanuts, coffee or other well established cash crops. This will be accomplished by selling the seeds at subsidized rates and providing educational material on the benefits of cash crops. Additionally, new research will be started to investigate the possibility of converting rice paddies into algae ponds for use in bio-reactors and biodiesel production. This study will also investigate the feasibility of bio-diesel as an export.

Education

The education budget under the Junta was just below 20% of the annual budget. This will be reduced. There are many systemic problems that plague the education system in Thailand, for too long has more money just been thrown at the problem in order to resolve the problem. Instead funds will be allocated to a research program that will develop a new education system for the country that addresses the root of the problems and builds a new education system that better fits the needs of the country. Under the proposed plan, the cuts that are made will be at the higher levels of education ministry and the development budget of The Ministry of Education. This will attempt to minimize disruption in the education received by students.

Military

Thailand has a strong military tradition, something that the His Majesty is very proud of, the military will be expanded under the Grand Vision, additional funding will be allocated to increase pay within the ranks. The Grand Royal Vision also provides for an increase year after year in the procurement budget of the Royal Thai Military. This has been seen partially as a political move to ensure the loyalty of the military and to mitigate circumstances that would lead to another coup.

Internal Reforms

The final set of reforms focus on the police and governmental bodies. The Grand Royal Vision provides additional funding to increase salaries of police officers. The Police force will be removed from the control of the ministry of defense and placed under the control of the ministry of the interior. Additionally, the internal investigations branch will be separated from the police force and form the new body investigative body titled the “Royal Thai Investigative Taskforce.” The director of this organization will report directly to the Privy Council and the King. This organization will be charged with discovering corruption and subversion within the military, the police and the government and bringing those individuals to justice.
